articles.title: Nazareth's defense dominates Providence, which loses its first game after firing Tyler Plantz
articles.description:
Two teams facing a midseason gut-check met up on Friday in LaGrange Park.

No. 5 Providence spent the past week in a media firestorm after the school fired head coach Tyler Plantz. The unusual mid-season coaching change caught the attention of casual sports fans and the local television media.

For Nazareth, the problems this season have all been on the field. The Roadrunners were highly touted in the preseason but lost three of their first four games. The defeats were to good teams, and Nazareth is missing several of its top players to injuries, but the season risked heading down a negative path with another loss.

“Our two senior captains have been injured, and we have had a lot of adversity against us,” Nazareth receiver Jackson Flickenger said. “We had meetings all this week about staying together, and we took that super seriously.”

The No. 22 Roadrunners dominated defensively and pulled out a 17-7 victory. It was Providence's first loss of the season, now helmed by interim head coach Adam Nissen, previously the team’s offensive coordinator.

Nissen acknowledged before the game that a loss was likely to fan the flames of controversy that started on Sunday when Providence announced Plantz’s firing. But he isn’t worried about how his team will handle the defeat internally.

“Our senior group is awesome,” Nissen said. “I have no doubt we will bounce back. We will watch some film and get ready. We will be ready next week.”

The Celtics (4-1) had a chance to cut the deficit to one possession when they recovered an onside kick with 8:40 left, trailing 17-7.

But junior defensive lineman John Bukovac stepped up with a big sack on the next play. And junior linebacker Harry Keenan grabbed an interception on fourth down with just more than a minute to play that sealed the win.

“We had to stay locked in as a team and trust each other and get it done,” Keenan said.

Sean Trayser and Henry Walz had interceptions for Nazareth in the first half.

“The defense was excellent,” Roadrunners coach Tim Racki said. “Especially with the weapons Providence has. Their running game is lethal.”

Second INT of the game for Nazareth. Henry Walz grabs the tipped pass.

Roadrunners and Providence scoreless in the 2Q. pic.twitter.com/I5XaGiCYQn

— Michael O'Brien (@michaelsobrien) September 18, 2026

But Nazareth’s running game stole the show. Charles Calhoun put the Roadrunners (2-3) ahead 17-0 with a six-yard TD run to cap off a drive that sucked up most of the third quarter.

“That was like a 10-minute drive,” Calhoun said. “I could feel it. We were on a roll. Once we get on a high, there is no taking us down.”

Calhoun had 24 carries for 103 yards, and Jack Parisi added 14 carries for 77 yards.

Nazareth quarterback JJ Chapman was 7-for-16 passing for 89 yards. He threw a 34-yard touchdown pass to Charles Heck late in the first half. Flickenger had five catches for 42 yards.

“We really came to play a complete football game,” Racki said. “And that is hard to do after an emotional loss last week. Our kids had an edge all week.”

Providence running back Broden Mackert had 17 carries for 123 yards and one touchdown. Celtics quarterback Dominic Vita went 13 of 20 for 90 yards with three interceptions.

“We definitely knew they had been through some adversity this week with their coach being fired,” Calhoun said. “We came out hard. We knew it would be a game to fight for and we wanted to use that to our advantage.”

Nazareth limited media access to the game, and no television cameras or independent videographers were present.

Otherwise, it was business as usual for Providence despite all the controversy around Plantz’s firing. A handful of Celtics fans in the crowd wore white T-shirts that read “We support coach Plantz.”

“We left too many plays on the field,” Nissen, who was previously a head coach at St. Laurence, said. “A couple turnovers; didn’t execute like we normally do. We had a good week of practice and were pretty locked in on what we were trying to do. We had the opportunities at the end of the game; we just couldn’t capitalize on it.”

articles.title: 8 PC gaming upgrades under $100 that are actually worth it
articles.description: Gaming on a budget doesn’t have to mean compromising on quality. Whether you’re a casual player or a dedicated enthusiast, finding the right accessories can make the precious hours you get to spend in front of your computer that much better... without emptying your wallet. We’ve dug around and found some of the best PC gaming accessories under $100. Not only will you get top-notch performance, but you’ll get great value too. Let’s dive into the gear that proves great gaming doesn’t have to come with a hefty price tag. Upgrade your mouse: Razer Basilisk V3 X HyperSpeed Razer One of the main things you need for your gaming setup is a proper mouse. There are so many options out there, but we’re particularly in love with the Razer Basilisk V3 X HyperSpeed . With an 18K optical sensor, nine programmable keys, and Chroma RGB, this one’s speedy, versatile, and gorgeous. The Basilisk V3 is also a solid option with a 26K DPI optical sensor and 11 programmable buttons. If you’re into MMOs, then the Naga V2 HyperSpeed may be better with its 19 buttons and 30K sensor. Get the Razer Basilisk V3 X HyperSpeed at Amazon Get the Razer Basilisk V3 at Amazon Get the Razer Naga V2 HyperSpeed at Amazon Elevate your laptop while expanding its ports: Mukiya USB-C Dock Stand Mukiya If you’re on a gaming laptop, then you’ll get a ton of mileage out of a USB-C laptop docking station stand like this one by Mukiya . Not only does it support nine different angles, but it also has an integrated dock with ports for 4K HDMI, two USB-A, one USB-C for data, one USB-C with 85W of passthrough charging, as well as SD and microSD card slots. It’s the ultimate accessory for a decked-out gaming laptop. Get the Mukiya USB-C Dock Stand at Amazon Add more screens and accessories to your laptop: Anker 14-in-1 Docking Station Anker If you want an even more versatile docking station than the Mukiya above and you don’t need the laptop stand feature, then this Anker 14-in-1 Laptop Docking Station is a great option. It comes with two 4K HDMI ports and another 1080p VGA port, enabling you to add three displays to your gaming laptop. It also has several USB ports, a USB-C PD port with 100W max charging power, SD and microSD card slots, and a Gigabit Ethernet port for stable online gaming. Get the Anker 14-in-1 Docking Station at Amazon Upgrade your audio quality: Creative Pebble Pro Desktop Speakers Creative Laptops (and monitors) don’t come with high-quality integrated speakers, so you’re going to need a proper pair if you want to properly enjoy the movies and TV shows you watch and the games you play. For their price, these Creative Pebble Pro Desktop Speakers are absolute gold. They have a minimalist design, they come with Bluetooth 5.3 support, and they have customizable RGB lighting. Get the Creative Pebble Pro at Amazon Chat online in ultimate comfort: Turtle Beach Stealth 600 Wireless Headset Dominic Bayley / IDG If you’re into online multiplayer games, then you need to be able to keep in touch with friends on Discord. The Turtle Beach Stealth 600 Wireless Headset is one of our favorites, not only for PC gaming but also while working, while on your phone, and even while gaming on the Xbox One and PS5. It delivers up to 80 hours of battery on a single charge, has a noise-cancelling mic, and it’s super comfy. While its MSRP is usually over $100, you can often get it on sale for below that. Get the Turtle Beach Stealth 600 at Amazon Organize your controllers: Razer Controller Charging Stand Razer I love gaming on a PC with a proper controller, but keeping those controllers charged can be a chore most days. Well, not if you get one of these Razer charging stands that double as a charger and a stand to rest your controller while it’s recharging. You’ll need to grab either the Xbox version or PS5 version depending on what you have. Get the Razer Charging Stand (Xbox) at Amazon Get the Razer Charging Stand (PS5) at Amazon Get a better keyboard: Logitech G413 SE Gaming Keyboard Logitech Gaming keyboards are great for gamers, obviously. They’re speedy, comfortable for long sessions, backlit so you can find the keys even when gaming at night, and deliciously tactile. The Logitech G413 SE is a full-sized keyboard that features PBT keycaps that are resistant to both heat and wear and tear. There are also 12 function keys available to control media, toggle lighting, and more. While there are so many other gaming keyboards we could recommend, this one’s a good value pick because it’s from a top brand yet still well under $100. Get the Logitech G413 SE at Amazon Perfect your monitor ergonomics: Huanuo FlowLift Dual Monitor Arms HUANUO Monitor arms serve double duty: they lift your monitors up to free up precious desk space, and they raise them to proper height with precise adjustments to minimize eye strain and poor posture. The Huanuo FlowLift Dual Monitor Arms are ideal for dual-monitor setups, with two independent arms that each tilt, swivel, and rotate as needed. Each arm can hold monitors from 13 to 32 inches and up to 19.8 pounds. In this price range, these arms are nigh unbeatable. Get the Huanuo FlowLift Dual Monitor Arms at Amazon
